newsitem.title: USA: Colgate shares up on bullish FY97 outlook.
newsitem.headline: Colgate shares up on bullish FY97 outlook.

text.p: Colgate-Palmolive Co shares shot up to a 52-week high Tuesday on news the company is bullish about its 1997 performance and comfortable with the range of $4.70 per share to $4.85 per share for the year.
"They seemed very comfortable with the range," said Michael Grant, a J.P. Morgan analyst. "It looks like they are poised for a very strong year."
Colgate declined to comment on the annual estimates.
The company was up 2-3/8 to 98-5/8 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
The global consumer products giant said Tuesday morning it posted fourth-quarter net income of $181.7 million, or $1.20 per share, compared with $122.5 million, or $0.80 per share, last year.
It beat the First Call estimate of $1.19 per share by a penny.
Analysts said the company reiterated its strong showing in both top-line and margin growth during its conference call.
The company also told analysts it expected its Total toothpaste to be cleared for U.S. release in the second half of the year, perhaps in the third quarter.

The company has been waiting many months for the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to approve the marketing of Total as a treatment for gingivitis, plaque, tartar and cavities. It originally was expected at the end of 1996, then the first quarter of 1997.
Still, analysts said the company's results were promising.

"Results were solid across all divisions," Heather Hay, a Prudential Securities analyst, said in her research report. "Margins also continue to improve, even as Colgate ups their advertising efforts."
Analysts said they expected to see gross margin strength throughout the year.
The company whose products include Colgate toothpaste, Palmolive soap, Ajax detergent and Speed Stick deodorant, said gross profit margin increased by 170 basis points in the quarter to 49.6 percent.
